# A product of two-limb numbers with a bound of its error

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `mul_ball_2_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $z$ of $x y$ with a bound $d$ of its error:

$$\lvert (x y) - z\rvert \le d.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $y = y_0 + y_1$, $z = z_0 + z_1$.

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`mul_dir_2_2`](mul_dir_2_2.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.
- $y$ is normalized: $y_0 = \mathrm{RN}(y_0 + y_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z$ is normalized: $z_0 = \mathrm{RN}(z_0 + z_1)$.
- $\lvert z - x y\rvert \le 4\,u^2\,\lvert x y\rvert + \tfrac{3}{2}\,\eta$.
- $\lvert (x y) - z\rvert \le d$: $d$ bounds the error of $z$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u^2$ | $2^{-104} \approx 4.9304 \times 10^{-32}$ | $2^{-46} \approx 1.4211 \times 10^{-14}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $3 \cdot 2^{-1075} \approx 7.411 \times 10^{-324}$ | $3 \cdot 2^{-150} \approx 2.1019 \times 10^{-45}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1p-104`, `0x1p-1073` | `0x1p-46f`, `0x1p-148f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0x1.0000000000001p-104`, `0x1p-1073` | `0x1.000002p-46f`, `0x1p-148f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 4 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `mul_ball_2_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Directed2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Directed2.v), against `mul_ball_2_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions mul_ball_2_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition mul_ball_2_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (4 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 y0 y1 : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  normalized_2 emin prec y0 y1 ->
  let '(z0, z1, d) := mul_ball_2_2 emin prec tie_even x0 x1 y0 y1 in
  fmt emin prec d /\
  normalized_2 emin prec z0 z1 /\
  Rabs ((z0 + z1) - ((x0 + x1) * (y0 + y1))) <= 4 * u prec ^ 2 * Rabs ((x0 + x1) * (y0 + y1)) + (3 / 2) * eta emin /\
  Rabs (((x0 + x1) * (y0 + y1)) - (z0 + z1)) <= d.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `mul_ball_2_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** mul_2_2 with the radius of ball_mul_2 for radii zero (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/mul_ball_2_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/mul_ball_2_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`mul_2_2`](mul_2_2.md).

```
# The product of two 2-limb numbers with a bound d of its own error, |x y - z| <= d
# (milestone2.md, "Interval kernels", "Bounds of two limbs"). d is the radius that ball_mul_2
# returns for radii zero, with the same three constants E, G, H: there p, q and w are roundings of
# zero and t = fma(az, E, 0), which is prod(az, E). So the statement is ball_mul_2_correct after two
# rewritings, with the error bound of mul_2_2 for z. The operands are points: the encloses claim
# names no ball.

(z0, z1) = mul_2_2(x0, x1, y0, y1)
az       = abs(z0)
t        = prod(az, const up(unit(mul_2_2)/(1-unit(mul_2_2))))
d        = fma(t, const up((1+u)^6), const up((1+u)*(2*(1+u)^5*eta+tiny(mul_2_2)/(1-unit(mul_2_2))+eta/2)+eta/(2*u)))
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#mul_ball_2_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | smallest slack of the radius, in gaps | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 6 643 314 | 0 | 0.949708 | 2.12668e+15 | no |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 6 634 296 | 0 | 0.942075 | 2.57199e+6 | no |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 11 398 817 | 0 | 0.898829 (`fp:6:-7:-3`) | 7.03516 (`fp:4:-9:-3`) | no |

The slack is how far the returned radius is above the smallest radius that encloses the exact set, in units in the last place of the radius: below 1, a radius one unit smaller would not enclose it.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
